title: CLI
levelTitle: Level 28 - Cisco IOS and IOS XE

cards.a: The primary configuration interface for IOS and IOS XE. Exec commands (like show and ping) run in privileged mode; configure commands (like interface and router) run in config mode. It includes built-in help, tab completion, and the do command to run EXEC commands from any mode.

cards.q: Which two command classes exist in the Cisco CLI, and where does each run?
cards.a: EXEC commands run in user or privileged mode (for example show and ping); configure commands run in configuration mode (for example interface and router).

cards.q: What is the difference between typing ? with a space and ? with no space after a word?
cards.a: ? with a space lists commands or subcommands, which is context help (for example show ?). ? with no space completes the word and shows possible completions (for example show co?).

cards.q: Which keyboard shortcuts complete a word, recall history, exit config mode, abort, and interrupt output?
cards.a: Tab completes a word, Up arrow recalls command history, Ctrl+Z exits config mode (the same as end), Ctrl+C aborts, and Ctrl+Shift+6 interrupts an operation.

cards.q: What does the do command allow you to do?
cards.a: The do command runs an EXEC command, such as show or ping, from inside configuration mode without leaving it.

cards.q: What do privilege levels 0, 1, and 15 mean?
cards.a: 0 is minimal access, 1 is user mode, and 15 is privileged mode (enable, full access). Custom levels are created with the privilege command.

cards.q: Which show commands verify the live config, saved config, image, and interface status?
cards.a: show running-config shows the live config, show startup-config shows the saved config, show version shows the image and uptime, and show interfaces shows interface status. terminal length 0 disables output paging.

cards.q: What do the output modifiers | include, | exclude, | section, | begin, and | redirect do?
cards.a: | include X shows only lines containing X, | exclude X hides lines containing X, | section X shows the block containing X, | begin X starts output at X, and | redirect saves the output to a location such as tftp:.

cards.q: What is the purpose of the enable, configure terminal, no, and end commands?
cards.a: enable enters privileged mode (level 15), configure terminal enters global config mode, no removes or disables a setting, and end returns to privileged EXEC from config mode (same as Ctrl+Z).

cards.q: Why does the % Ambiguous error appear?
cards.a: The typed abbreviation matches more than one possible command. Type more characters so the command becomes unambiguous.

cards.q: What does the % Invalid input error mean?
cards.a: The command uses wrong syntax or was entered in the wrong mode. Check the prompt and the command spelling.

cards.q: Why can you not configure an interface even though the command looks correct?
cards.a: The device is not in config mode, or the privilege level is below 15. Enter configure terminal from privileged EXEC before interface commands; without level 15 privilege you cannot reach config mode.
